design.title: Cross-survey DINOv2 distillation: each member's 8x8 feature map must reproduce a frozen foundation-model teacher's description of the SAME place photographed in a DIFFERENT survey (training-only; the teacher never flies)
design.init_strategy: from-scratch (deployed student unchanged); training-only teacher pretrained:dinov2_vits14_reg (Apache-2.0, torch.hub facebookresearch/dinov2), never exported
design.eli5: We hired a tutor. A large, freely licensed vision model that has already looked at hundreds of millions of photographs describes a scene by its roads, buildings and water, not by the colour cast, the season or where the shadows fall. During training only, our tiny navigator is shown one survey's photo of a spot and asked to produce the description the tutor gives for a DIFFERENT survey's photo of that same spot, so anything that changes between surveys is useless to it and only the layout pays. A measurement on the three training surveys shows the tutor recognises a place across surveys even when the view is shifted 12 m, where raw pixels fail nine times out of ten. The tutor never flies: what stays on the drone is exactly the same small model as before, now trained to see the city the way the tutor does.
design.hypothesis: Through seven experiments on this ruler the held-out 2024 photograph's usable-fix rate has never left the 7-12.5% band (exp 2: 7.0%, exp 4: 11.75%, exp 5: 12.5%, exp 6: 11.0%, exp 7: 7.5%) while everything around it moved: experiment 5 lifted the TRAINING photographs to 72-81% usable at the same held-out viewpoints and 2024 did not budge, and experiment 7's committee gate cut 2024 false fixes from 38.75% to 17% but, with coverage now 0.245 (floor 0.2), there is almost nothing left to convert. The score is 0.925 + 0.17 and the 0.925 is the whole problem: the deployed trunk, trained only on three photographs, does not produce a place description that a fourth photograph reproduces. Three in-domain surveys evidently do not teach that on their own (exp 3's agreement term was vacuous, exp 6's blends were reverted, exp 4's photometrics helped once), and every mechanism tried so far derived the representation from the three photographs themselves. This experiment imports one from outside: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 with registers (Apache-2.0, 22M parameters, library L2 rank 3, the 'largest documented effect in the scene-coordinate literature' per R-SCoRe/ACE-G) is used as a frozen TRAINING-ONLY teacher, and each committee member's 8x8 trunk feature map is trained, through a training-only projector, to match the teacher's 8x8 patch-token grid of the same position and heading in a DIFFERENT training survey (TSCM's cross term). Design-stage evidence, measured on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp8_dinov2.py, 300 random lattice places, teacher at 112 px, nearest-neighbour place retrieval across surveys; the 2024 capture was never opened): with the raw pixels, experiment 6's probe found a place across surveys 90-97% of the time when pixel-aligned but 7-11% under a 12 px shift and 1% under shift+rotation. DINOv2's centred patch grid finds it 95.2% aligned, 70.4% under the same 12 px shift (7-10x the pixel figure) and 22.9% under shift+rotation (23x), and the teacher's own cross-survey cosine between the same place in two surveys is 0.46-0.53 against 0.05 for different places. So the teacher's description of a place survives a change of survey AND the off-lattice shift the eval imposes, which the raw pixels do not; rotation tolerance is not in the teacher and stays the student's job (it trains under random headings, as before). The cross-survey pairing is what makes the target survey-invariant rather than merely semantic: the student sees survey A's augmented crop and must produce what the teacher says about survey B's clean crop of the same ground, so canopy, shadow direction, cars and colour pipeline, which differ between A and B, cannot help it and the shared geometry can. The student is the SAME exported model as experiment 7 (3,942,411 bytes); only the training loss changes. Two known limits are honest unknowns: whether a 0.97M-parameter two-member student can absorb enough of a 22M teacher's geometry (no published distillation result below 4M parameters), and whether the 14 m patch granularity at 112 px is right for a 128 m cell head. Cost: the teacher runs online, no cache; a ViT-S forward at 112 px is ~2.9 GFLOP, ~0.6 PFLOP per epoch of 218k views, a few tens of seconds on the L4 the loop trains on (REMOTE_TRAIN=1); measured 296 img/s on the M1 (12 min/epoch) if a run ever falls back to local training.
